routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: Ĝ-valued deformation theory and potential automorphy
routes.brief:
Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne prove the **converse** direction of the global Langlands correspondence over a function field, potentially and for every reductive group: for X smooth projective geometrically connected over F_q, G split semisimple with dual group Ĝ, and σ : π_1(X) → Ĝ(Q̄_l) continuous with **Zariski dense image**, there is a finite Galois K′/K and an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic Π of G(A_{K′}) matched with σ|_{W_{K′_v}} at every place under unramified local Langlands (Theorem 1.1 = Theorem 11.1). For groups of exceptional type this is the first theorem of its kind. The parent roadmap owns the automorphic side and V. Lafforgue’s automorphic-to-Galois direction (GS.0–GS.5, sourced from PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18); this Part II owns the Galois-to-automorphic machinery for the same objects.

Import, never re-plan:
- **GS.5** for V. Lafforgue’s excursion operators, the pseudocharacter Θ_{U(N)} valued in the excursion algebra B, and the parameters σ_p attached to its primes; **GS.7** for the local–global compatibility of Genestier–Lafforgue quoted as Theorem 8.9; **FA.6** for cuspidal functions on G(K)\\G(A_K)/U with their reduction-theoretic finiteness (Harder) and the unramified Satake dictionary; **FA.5** for Chebotarev over a function field in Chavdarov’s quantitative form; **RG2.5** for the dual group over Z and the L-group.
- **DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1–R03.5** for complete local coefficient categories, representability, the dimension/depth inequalities and the abstract patching module; **SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1, SR.2, SR.4** for Hecke algebras over rings, normalized induction and Jacquet functors, and the Satake transform; **LanglandsParameterStacks LP2/LP3** and **IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0/IHG.1** for the invariant theory and the pseudocharacter theory, both routed as sources by this same extraction; **ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.1** for integral models of continuous representations; **PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.1** for Moret-Bailly.

Construct, in the order the proof uses them:
- **Ĝ-valued deformation theory** (§5): the functor Def_{ρ̄} for ρ̄ absolutely Ĝ-irreducible, pro-represented by R_{ρ̄} because Ĝ^{ad,∧}_O acts freely on liftings, with the Mazur presentation by h¹ generators and h² relations; for Γ = Γ_{K,S} the Euler characteristic gives h¹ = h², so R_{ρ̄,S} is a complete intersection, and Weil II purity ([Laf02, Thm. VII.6], [Del80]) makes Spec R_{ρ̄,S}[1/l] formally unramified over E. Then Theorems 5.13–5.14: R_{ρ̄,S} is a reduced finite flat complete intersection and characteristic-zero lifts exist — the Khare–Wintenberger method in this setting, whose engine is **de Jong’s conjecture** as proved by Gaitsgory.
- **Taylor–Wiles data for Ĝ** (§5.3): places with ρ̄(Frob_v) regular semisimple, q_v ≡ 1 mod l and connected centralizer, the diagonal shape of the universal deformation there, the group Δ_Q as the maximal l-power quotient of ∏T(k(v)), the O[Δ_Q]-algebra structure on R_{ρ̄,S∪Q}, the **Ĝ-abundance** condition, and the existence of data killing the dual Selmer group with the rank-corrected count g = h¹ + (r − 1)#Q.
- **Compatible systems of Ĝ-representations** (§6), with the explicit warning that Definition 6.1 is *provisional* unless the image is Zariski dense, the rigidity Proposition 6.4, existence and uniqueness through Chin’s independence-of-l theorem, and the image results: a number field of definition with Ĝ(Z_l)-image at a density-one set of split primes (Larsen, Snowden–Wiles) and the criterion that Ĝ(F_l) in the residual image forces Ĝ(Z_l) for l > 2 dim ĝ.
- **The local calculation at a Taylor–Wiles place** (§7): the pro-prime-to-l Iwahori level U_1, the algebra map O[T(K)_l] → H_{U_1}, the localization (Π^{U_0})_{m_{χ̄}} ≅ Π^U, and the two compatibility propositions 7.8–7.9 comparing the Hecke and Galois actions **through Ĝ-pseudocharacters**.
- **The integral excursion algebra** B(U, O), finite flat over O, with its residual representations σ̄_m (§8.2–8.3), the freeness of C_{cusp}(W, O)_m over O[U/W] — through the free action of the diamond group on the adelic double coset space and a Hecke operator annihilating all Eisenstein constituents — and then **Theorem 8.20: f_m : R_{σ̄_m,∅} ≅ B(U, O)_m with C_{cusp}(U, O)_m free over it**, by Taylor–Wiles patching. Corollary 8.21 is the automorphy lifting theorem, with its Whittaker refinement.
- **Potential automorphy** (§§9–11): the Moret-Bailly linking of two residual representations over a common extension, an auxiliary curve carrying a compatible system with full Ĝ(F_l)-monodromy — which is how the paper avoids families of “Ĝ-motives” — the **Coxeter parameters** of §10 with their rigidity, good reduction and Ĝ-abundance, their automorphy through Braverman–Gaitsgory’s geometric Eisenstein series together with Gaitsgory’s two appendices (cuspidality; non-vanishing of the first Whittaker coefficient), and finally the “chutes and ladders” argument of [Ell05] with the descent to the adjoint group (Proposition 11.2).

Keep the hypotheses visible: l ∤ q; l very good for Ĝ, and l > 2(dim V − 1) for the auxiliary representation, l > 2h − 2 for Coxeter parameters, l > 2 dim ĝ for the image criterion; Zariski density throughout; the scheme-theoretically trivial centralizer in Ĝ^{ad}, which for GL_n is Schur’s lemma but in general is **strictly stronger** than irreducibility; and K′ ≠ K — “One expects that this theorem should be true with K′ = K, but we are not able to prove this.”

Record what is conditional: §11.1 is explicitly informal, Proposition 11.5 assumes Conjecture 11.6 and a generalization of Theorem 11.1 that the paper does not prove, and Appendix B rests on Raskin’s preprint. Tests: GL_n/PGL_n must recover L. Lafforgue’s theorem with K′ = K; a torus must recover class field theory; the r = 0 count of Taylor–Wiles places must degenerate correctly.
routes.reason:
Every object here is a Ĝ-valued representation of the Galois group of a function field, or a space of automorphic forms on G over that function field, or V. Lafforgue’s excursion algebra acting on it — which is exactly what GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands constructs in GS.0–GS.5, and the theorem proved is the converse of GS.5’s. So this is new work in the parent roadmap’s direction, not a rebuild of it: GS.5 gives the map from automorphic representations to parameters, and this Part II gives, for Zariski-dense parameters, a cuspidal automorphic representation after a finite base change.

It is not a Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure, PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems or GlobalGaloisDeformations, although all three plan the analogous machinery: those roadmaps are written for **number fields** and for **GL_n or polarized** representations — PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure is explicitly “over CM fields” and built for Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne, with cohomology of locally symmetric spaces as its object; PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems is Hilbert–Blumenthal GL_2; GlobalGaloisDeformations says “over number fields” and its stages are polarized or determinant-variable. Their mathematics is imported here, not repeated, and the differences are structural rather than cosmetic: the Galois side is a pseudocharacter valued in an excursion algebra rather than a Hecke algebra acting on cohomology; h¹ = h² replaces a defect term; de Jong’s conjecture replaces p-adic Hodge theory as the source of characteristic-zero lifts; Ĝ-abundance replaces adequacy; the patched module is a space of adelic cusp forms; and the universally automorphic objects are Coxeter parameters via geometric Eisenstein series rather than CM or induced representations via the trace formula.

It is also distinct from the three Part IIs of the same parent already proposed: ShtukaSpecialCyclesAndHigherSiegelWeil (PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17, PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24) is about special cycles on shtuka moduli; ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange (PAPER-FENG-24) about Tate cohomology and cyclic base change with mod p coefficients; GlobalShtukasPartIIRamanujanArthur (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26) about Ramanujan/Arthur weight constraints. None touches deformation theory of Ĝ-valued representations or potential automorphy. The design job should nonetheless cross-reference PAPER-FENG-24, which uses the Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne reconstruction theorem for modular coefficients, and PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18, whose Proposition 10.10 was found by these four authors for use here.

LP2 owns the coarse quotient and the excursion presentation with “the relation to closed semisimple geometric orbits”, and LP3 is the atlas’s stage for **integral reductive invariant theory**. §3 of this paper is precisely that theory, and in a stronger form than the characteristic-zero statements that PAPER-LAFFORGUE-18 routes to the same two stages:
- **Over an algebraically closed field of any characteristic** (§3.1): the categorical quotient X⿰G with Seshadri’s properties, the three notions of Definition 3.3 — G-complete reducibility in the sense of Serre, G-irreducibility, strong reductivity — and Theorem 3.4, that the diagonal conjugation orbit of a tuple is closed iff the group it generates is G-completely reducible ([Ric88] with [BMR05, Thm. 3.1]) and stable iff it is G-irreducible; Proposition 3.6 realizing the semisimplification as a limit lim_{t→0}λ(t)gλ(t)^{-1} along a cocharacter, which is the invariant-theoretic form of Serre’s construction; and Proposition 3.7.
- **Separability and very good characteristic**: Theorem 3.8 ([BMRT10]), that in very good characteristic — or for a reductive pair — every closed subgroup has smooth scheme-theoretic centralizer, with the explicit table (l ∤ n+1 in type A_n, l ≠ 2, 3, 5 in the other types) and Lemma 3.9, that l prime to #W suffices. Every deformation-theoretic statement in the paper runs on this hypothesis.
- **Over a discrete valuation ring** (§3.2): Proposition 3.10 — finite type, normality, the bijection between closed orbits and K-points of the quotient for every algebraically closed O → K, closed images, and commutation of invariants with **flat** base change — together with the sharp warning that O[X]^G ⊗_O K and K[X_K]^{G_K} are **not** isomorphic in general, which is exactly the trap an integral parameter space must avoid; and Proposition 3.13, the special case of **Luna’s étale slice theorem in mixed characteristic**: for X smooth over O and x with closed orbit and scheme-theoretically trivial centralizer, X^{∧,x}/G^∧ ≅ (X⿰G)^{∧,π(x)}. Applied to X = Ĝ^n_O with Ĝ^{ad}_O acting by conjugation, this is what makes Theorem 4.10 — and hence the whole paper — work. Lemmas 3.11–3.12 (descent of étaleness along a finite equivariant morphism, and an étaleness criterion for intermediate integral closures) are the technical inputs. Proposition 8.3, Chevalley restriction Z[M̂]^{M̂} ≅ Z[T̂]^{W(M̂,T̂)} over **Z**, belongs with them.

IHG.0 constructs homogeneous polynomial laws and determinants D : A[G] → A with characteristic-polynomial identities, base change, restriction and **continuity criteria**; IHG.1 constructs the Cayley–Hamilton quotient and proves **reconstruction** — over an algebraically closed field up to semisimplification, and over a complete local ring when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation. That is the GL_n theory of Chenevier, Carayol and Rouquier. §4 of this paper is its replacement for a general reductive group, and the atlas has no notion of it:
- Definition 4.1, the **Ĝ-pseudocharacter**: a compatible family of algebra maps Z[Ĝ^n]^Ĝ → Map(Γ^n, A) satisfying the reindexing and multiplication axioms, with the flat-base-change reformulation (Remark 4.2) and its explicit failure for non-flat O, and the functorialities of Lemmas 4.3–4.4.
- Theorem 4.5: over an algebraically closed field of **any** characteristic, ρ ↦ tr ρ is a bijection from Ĝ(k)-conjugacy classes of Ĝ-completely reducible representations to Ĝ-pseudocharacters. This is V. Lafforgue’s theorem, reproved here because “some modifications are required in the case of positive characteristic”, and it is the statement LP2:semisimple-characters uses in its Fargues–Scholze local form: one proof should serve all three.
- Proposition 4.7, the continuity dictionary, with the discrete case (iii) that the mod-l theory needs and that does not follow from the characteristic-zero case (ii).
- Theorem 4.10, the paper’s **first main contribution**: if the centralizer of ρ̄ in Ĝ^{ad}_k is scheme-theoretically trivial and ρ̄ is absolutely Ĝ-completely reducible, then deforming the pseudocharacter is the same as deforming the representation, Def_{ρ̄} ≅ PDef_{Θ̄}. For GL_n the hypothesis is Schur’s lemma and the statement is Carayol’s; in general the hypothesis is strictly stronger, and it is what allows an integral form of Lafforgue’s excursion algebra to carry an actual Ĝ-valued representation. Its proof is the mixed-characteristic slice theorem routed to LP3.

R01.1 plans continuous representations and **integral models**: invariant lattices by compactness for field coefficients, and “reduction followed by semisimplification” with independence of the lattice by characteristic polynomials and Brauer–Nesbitt — all for GL_n. Theorem 4.8 is the Ĝ-valued analogue for an arbitrary profinite group: a continuous Ĝ-pseudocharacter over Q̄_l takes values in some O_E; a continuous ρ : Γ → Ĝ(Q̄_l) is conjugate into Ĝ(O_E); and the semisimplification of its reduction is a well-defined continuous ρ̄ : Γ → Ĝ(F̄_l) up to conjugacy (Definition 4.9). The proof is genuinely different from the lattice argument: Baire category to descend to Ĝ(E), then **Bruhat–Tits theory** — the building of the derived group, the subgroup Ĝ(E)⁰ of elements whose characters are units, maximal compacts as stabilizers of centroids of facets, and the hyperspecial vertex with stabilizer Ĝ(O_E) — together with [Lar95, Lemma 2.4] to find a totally ramified extension over which some ρ(Γ)-stable vertex becomes hyperspecial. No hypothesis on l is needed. R01.1 should state the general reductive case with this proof and specialize to GL_n, rather than the other way round.

R23.1, “Moret–Bailly’s theorem”, plans the rational-point existence theorem “for the smooth geometrically irreducible varieties used here, with prescribed nonempty local open sets and a finite extension satisfying the required disjointness and real-place conditions”, and insists on including “the geometric and approximation prerequisites of the theorem rather than citing it as an axiom”. §9 is the **function-field** instance, and it differs in every detail that matters: there are no real places, so the condition K′ ∩ F̄_q = F_q takes their place and is forced by choosing two places of coprime residue degree; the auxiliary variety is the isomorphism scheme Z_{ψ,φ} = Isom_{Y_K,H}(X_φ, X_ψ) of two H-torsors on a curve, whose geometric connectedness (Lemma 9.1) comes from the surjectivity of ψ on the geometric fundamental group via [SGA1, V.6.9]; local points exist at almost all places by spreading out and the Weil bounds; and the two inputs quoted from Moret-Bailly are [MB89, Théorème 1.3] for the S-split extension carrying a rational point (Proposition 9.2) and [MB90] for global fields with prescribed local Galois behaviour (Theorem 9.3, quoted without proof). Remark 9.4 points to Gan–Lomelí [GLa] for an automorphic analogue of Theorem 9.3, which R23.1 may want to record as a consumer.
